title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1969-01-25
lineage: SBD > MR > C > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Rough soundboard mix with an over‑loud organ and occasional synth overlay, but a legendary show highlighted by a scorching Dark Star, The Eleven, Alligator > Caution and Lovelight.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised as one of the band’s most innovative early‑’69 shows – Dark Star into Stephen Stills, an incendiary The Eleven, and a thunderous Alligator > Caution sequence that many call unforgettable.  The recording, however, suffers from a badly balanced mix: Tom Constanten’s (or TC’s) organ is way up front, vocals are often buried, Jerry’s guitar drops low, and there may be an added keyboard‑synth track on Dark Star.  Despite the technical flaws, fans consider it a must‑listen for its energy and improvisational fire.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is consistently rated 4‑5 stars with multiple rave comments about standout jams; recording quality is noted as poor to fair, pulling the weighted average down but still yielding a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mix is unbalanced – organ (TC) far too loud, vocals often buried until later in Lovelight, Jerry's guitar low on Dark Star, occasional synth/keyboard overlay that sounds like an added track. Early tracks have screwy mix; second set improves but still not pristine.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Early set hampered by mix issues but still energetic; second set shines with a classic Dark Star > Stephan > The Eleven > Lovelight sequence and an explosive Alligator‑Caution climax, showcasing the band’s exploratory peak of ’69.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar often buried in the mix but described as fantastic when audible; his tone praised on The Eleven and other jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals are generally clear later in the set; Bob’s vocal parts noted as audible despite overall mix problems.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten (TC) organ is excessively forward – likely a Vox Continental at this point, with occasional synth‑like overlay on Dark Star that some suspect is an added track.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill and Mickey are praised for playing “their A$$ off”; drum work noted as powerful throughout, especially on Alligator and Caution.
